These rule changes are essentially an expansion of the current regulatory framework, which now considers anyone who co-sponsors a defined contribution (DC) retirement plan, such as a 401(k), to be sharing in its fiduciary responsibility.
For the majority of small employers, the plan's requirement of contributing for administrative costs would prevent them from offering a DC plan, unless an administrative fee was waived. Ditto things like complying with statutory notice requirements, which fail to “reflect the reality that many employers receive only minimal, if any, financial benefit from participating in multiple-employer plans or adding individual employees.” The rule change would permit sponsors to align administration with the benefits employees received, as detailed in an additional notice that preceded the rise in plan-level contributions.
